_readme: Confirmed metric merges, decided one at a time with the user and recorded here.
Metric ids are the handbook's own row labels turned into slugs, so the same concept
arrives under several ids: a plural 's', a leading sub-item '(a)', or simply a
different table for life and general business. Merging them is a judgement about
what the concept IS, so each entry carries its evidence and the date it was agreed.
A merge is only made after checking the members never occupy the same
(insurer, year, line of business, class of business) slot. Zero overlap means the
ids are complementary halves of one metric and nothing is lost or double counted;
any overlap would mean they are genuinely different things.
Applied in memory, like the insurer aliases, because production restores its
database from the Litestream replica and never sees a local migration.

aliases.label: Interest, Dividend & Rent - Gross
why: One concept, gross investment income, arriving under three ids:
interest_dividend_rent_gross__inr     1,445 rows  'Interest, Dividend & Rent - Gross (Rs Crore)'
a_interest_dividends_rent_gross__inr    483 rows  '(a) Interest, Dividends & Rent - Gross (Rs Lakh)'  [life tables]
a_interest_dividend_rent_gross__inr     420 rows  '(a) Interest, Dividend & Rent - Gross (Rs Crore)'  [shareholders account]
They differ by a plural 's', a sub-item '(a)', and which table they came from.
None of that is identity: the sub-item letter is a position in a printed list, and
the life/general split is already carried by insurer_class.
